author: claude independent technology SME critic (jdbc-data-access recheck 2026-11-09)

findings.claim: t3Check rejects any occurrence of setAutoCommit(true), so a correct transfer that restores auto-commit in a finally block (the pattern in Oracle's own Using Transactions tutorial) fails with 'true keeps auto-commit on, so each update is saved on its own'. That message is false for a finally placed after commit/rollback.
findings.recommendation: Only flag setAutoCommit(true) when it appears before the last executeUpdate or before conn.commit(); accept it after the catch (for example in a finally block) and optionally mention restoring auto-commit as good practice for pooled connections.

findings.claim: The rethrow regex only requires the catch variable as a whole word somewhere inside new X(...), so it accepts wrappers that drop the cause, e.g. throw new RuntimeException(e.getMessage()); or throw new IllegalStateException("bad e");, contradicting the page's own rule 'wrap it in a new exception that keeps it as the cause'.
findings.recommendation: Require the bare catch variable as a constructor argument (e.g. new X(e) or new X("...", e): match [(,]\s*e\s*\) ), not e.getMessage() or e inside a string literal; keep accepting throw e; and throw new RuntimeException(e);.
